chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad Al-Zayyat, who said:
I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'I performed Zihar with my wife.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'How did you say it?' I said, 'I said to her,

key_terms.أَبِى الْحَسَنِ: Abu Al-Hasan (Imam Al-Reza, peace be upon him)
key_terms.ظَاهَرْتُ: I performed Zihar (likening wife to mother)
key_terms.كَظَهْرِ أُمِّى: Like the back of my mother (the formula for Zihar)
key_terms.لَا شَىْءَ عَلَيْكَ: There is nothing upon you (no penalty due)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on Zihar if one says 'You are to me like the back of my mother'?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the juristic principle that Zihar requires specific verbal formulation to take effect, as the Imam (peace be upon him) ruled no expiation was due for the stated formula. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on precise linguistic intent (niyyah) in marital jurisprudence, distinguishing between the act of declaration and the subsequent obligation of kaffarah. The instruction 'do not repeat' serves as a preventive measure to avoid triggering the legal consequences of Zihar.
